name: Workshop - Volta Industrial (Downtime & Maintenance Rescue)
narrative:
Sam Ortiz, a non-technical VP of Manufacturing Operations, opens the plant-floor view and sees what the line supervisors have been watching for three weeks: a cluster of production lines glowing red — vibration and temperature telemetry trending toward failure, work-order backlogs, and parts that would have to be expedited if a line goes down unplanned. The nightly report surfaces it after the shift, when the stop has already cost $22K an hour.

Sam asks about the worst line: LINE-04 at the Ohio plant, failure-risk score 0.87 and climbing, with the replacement part not stocked locally. Pull it now or run it to the end of the shift? The assistant ranks the three plays (pull now for planned maintenance, run to end of shift and accept the unplanned-stop risk, or expedite the part and run), each with the expected downtime cost, parts cost, and SLA exposure, from a heuristic scored on Volta's own maintenance and failure history. It recommends pulling the line now, drafts the work order, and stops for approval. Sam approves; the work order writes back to Lakebase with an audit trail — governed telemetry turned into a floor action, scoped to the one plant, with the assistant's AI spend capped and predictable per plant across the fleet of eight.

Workshop training template (Tech Summit FY27 Live Days): data generator + full spec set (SDP pipeline, metric views, failure-risk model, dashboard + Genie, and a Databricks App with a Visualize/Assist/Act agent loop over Lakebase). Maps to the three build milestones — Lakebase, Databricks Apps, Unity AI Gateway.
